stem: For resistant cases of night terrors, what is the recommended procedure for 'scheduled awakenings'?

options.text: Wake the child $10-15$ minutes before the typical event time for $5-7$ nights
Wake the child immediately when the night terror begins to shorten its duration
Maintain the child in an awake state for at least $30$ minutes after an awakening
Administer a mild sedative $30$ minutes before the scheduled awakening

explanation: This technique involves disrupting the sleep cycle just before the anticipated terror to prevent the transition that triggers the episode.
rationale: This method relies on preemptive timing based on a recorded history of the episodes.

optionExplanations.A: This technique involves disrupting the sleep cycle just before the anticipated terror to prevent the transition that triggers the episode.
optionExplanations.B: Attempting to wake a child during a night terror is discouraged as it can actually 'ramp up' or prolong the agitation.
optionExplanations.C: The source suggests maintaining an awake state for only about $5$ minutes during the scheduled awakening procedure.
optionExplanations.D: Medications are generally not recommended for night terrors; the focus is on behavioral management and sleep hygiene.
